_comment: AOCL state-based run summary — the CR-012 reference run (aocl-engine-statebased on execution-definition-statebased-sim + canonical-loop vectors GD3/DV3/FI3 + scenario-library-sim SCN-SIM-BASELINE-001, seed 2026). The invariant suite (S1-S8, multi-seed S6) evaluates as run verdicts: 7/7 hold; the four formal-model findings are reported as observations (SBE-013). SimulationEvidence carries run identity, seed, vectors, engine version.

invariants.statement: peak severity decreases monotonically L1→L5 (bounded); MTTR drops sharply L1→L2 and stays bounded — recovery speed in the HITL/HOTL band is human-policy-driven, not a maturity law
human burden decreases L1→L4; L5 bounded (novelty-only engagement)
L3 pre-empts known modes (count < 0.8x L2); novel depth L3≈L2; L4 depth < L3
invariants.detail: known_count L2=19 L3=3; novel_depth L2=15.79 L3=14.05 L4=6.54

invariants.statement: level does not prevent velocity-mismatch excursions (prevention rate < 15% at L1 AND L5)
invariants.detail: prevented fraction: L1=0% L5=0% — L5-slow human_ticks=0 (HOOTL watches only novel/self; accumulation is silent — velocity fit is load-bearing for L5)

invariants.statement: L5 experimentation is sandboxed: zero self-inflicted production excursions
invariants.detail: quiet: L4 self=1 vs L5 self=0 (unsandboxed experimentation raised L5 human burden above L4 in an earlier iteration — assumption 7 must be explicit in the formal model)

invariants.statement: governing slow loop's playbook conversion cuts mean epoch-2 excursion count by >=30% (8-seed mini-study; exception upflow → policy downflow)
invariants.detail: mean epoch2 count: governed=4.25 ungoverned=15.25 (samples with/without: [3, 3, 5, 5, 4, 3, 6, 5] / [19, 17, 15, 11, 16, 19, 11, 14])

invariants.statement: DV 5→2 at the same L5 shape: zero-touch lost (human burden >= 2x) and MTTR >= 1.5x
invariants.detail: human 30→780 (26.0x); mttr 2.14→8.55 (4.0x); excursions 42→69 (missed detections aggregate onsets)

formalFindings.statement: L5 does not extend the burden monotonicity: with humans out of the loop, routine recovery is the loop's alone (its MTTR can exceed L4's human-assisted recovery), and novelty/deployment events still summon people. The formal model should say L5 eliminates ROUTINE burden — not that burden monotonically decreases to zero.
Under min-aggregation, (GD5,DV1,FI5) is behaviorally IDENTICAL to pure L1 — the model cannot express 'sophisticated but blind'. Is that the intended semantics?
formalFindings.detail: blind-savant == pure L1 exactly: False (mttr 22.85, peak 53.2, human 2160)

formalFindings.statement: Conversely, (GD5,DV2,FI5) — also min-L2 — BEHAVES BETTER than pure L2 (FI4+ gain adaptation is vector-gated, not level-gated). min-aggregation is inconsistent: it gates some capabilities but not others. Decision needed: strictly level-gate all capabilities, or treat (GD,DV,FI) as the behavioral profile and 'level' as a reporting label only.
formalFindings.detail: savant(peak=46.37, mttr=8.26, human=840) vs pure-L2(peak=42.54, mttr=8.65, human=840)

formalFindings.statement: Level policy parameters (gain, thresholds, lead times) are velocity-independent in the mapping. Any instability of high-gain policies on slow cycles is a formal-model gap: the mapping needs an explicit gain×cycle co-design rule (or a velocity-fit precondition before high maturity is claimed).
formalFindings.detail: slow-L5 mttr=2860.0 peak=721.78 (compare fast-L5 in S1)
